title: Nous Research Hits $1.5B Valuation, Launches AI Agents
summary: Nous Research confirms $1.5B valuation with $90M Series B, officially launching Hermes Agent for business users. A major milestone for the AI startup.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Nous Research reached a $1.5 billion valuation after closing a $90 million Series B funding round.
- The company officially launched Hermes Agent, a business-focused AI agent platform for enterprise users.
- This positions Nous Research as a major player in the competitive AI agent market for businesses.


Nous Research has confirmed it achieved a $1.5 billion valuation following a $90 million Series B funding round, while simultaneously launching Hermes Agent, a new AI agent platform designed specifically for business users. Officially released on October 7, 2026, the platform marks a significant expansion of the company's reach beyond research-focused applications into mainstream enterprise deployment.


## Funding Milestone and Market Position


The Series B round positions Nous Research among the fastest-growing AI startups, with the $1.5 billion valuation reflecting strong investor confidence in the company's technology and market potential. According to the official announcement, the funding will support expanded engineering teams, infrastructure scaling, and go-to-market initiatives for Hermes Agent. The company has not disclosed lead investors or participation details, but the substantial raise signals institutional backing at a competitive valuation multiple.


## Hermes Agent Platform Details


Hermes Agent represents Nous Research's first major product targeting business users directly, moving beyond the company's traditional developer and research audiences. The platform enables organizations to deploy autonomous AI agents for workflow automation, data analysis, and decision support tasks. Key capabilities reportedly include:


- Multi-step reasoning and task decomposition for complex business processes
- Integration with common enterprise software and data sources
- Customizable agent behaviors aligned with organizational policies
- Real-time monitoring and audit trails for compliance requirements


The launch targets mid-market and enterprise customers seeking to implement[AI agents for business](https://emergent.sh/learn/ai-agents-for-small-business) without requiring extensive machine learning expertise from internal teams.


## Release Date and Availability


Nous Research officially launched Hermes Agent on October 7, 2026, with general availability for enterprise customers. The platform is accessible through a web-based console and API, with pricing reportedly structured around usage tiers and deployment scale. Early access customers have been testing the platform since mid-2026, according to sources familiar with the rollout.


## Competitive Landscape


The launch places Nous Research in direct competition with established enterprise AI platforms and recent entrants focusing on[business automation agents](https://emergent.sh/learn/best-ai-agents-for-business) . The company's differentiation centers on its research pedigree and claimed performance advantages in reasoning tasks, though independent benchmarks have not yet been published. Market analysts note that the $1.5 billion valuation reflects both the platform's technical capabilities and the broader investor appetite for AI infrastructure companies serving enterprise customers.


## What This Means


Nous Research's funding and product launch represent a strategic pivot from pure research toward commercialization, joining a crowded field of AI agent platforms competing for enterprise budgets. The $1.5 billion valuation and substantial Series B raise provide runway for aggressive scaling, but success will depend on Hermes Agent's ability to deliver measurable ROI in production business environments. For organizations evaluating[AI agent solutions](https://emergent.sh/ai-agent-builder/business-automation) , the platform offers a new option backed by significant capital and technical expertise, though adoption will likely hinge on early customer results and competitive pricing relative to established alternatives.
